subject.title: WhatsApp QR-unavailable/headless login needs phone-code fallback

question: Should WhatsApp phone-code login be exposed through the generic `ChannelAuthAdapter` and `openclaw channels login --phone-number`, or should the entrypoint stay WhatsApp-owned?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful and vision-aligned, but the linked implementations add a public CLI flag and plugin-facing auth contract for a channel-specific login method, which is a product/API boundary choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Fix
options.body: Keep the typed generic login-method seam and require the Baileys pairing-code fix plus live/upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Move To WhatsApp-Owned Surface
options.body: Rework the CLI/API so phone-code login is owned by the WhatsApp plugin without expanding the generic channel-auth contract.

options.title: Pause Until Dependency Direction Settles
options.body: Defer landing until maintainers choose or vendor the pairing-safe Baileys behavior needed for reliable phone-code login.

recommendation.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the typed generic login-method seam and require the Baileys pairing-code fix plus live/upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses public CLI, plugin SDK, docs, and channel-auth boundaries where recent history points to steipete as the best routing owner.
